legal.crossBorderTitle: Cross-Border Health Data Transfer Disclosure Statement
legal.retentionTitle: Personal Health Data Retention and Destruction Policy
legal.privacyHtml:
1. Data Controller

As the data controller, Alumas Health Technologies Inc. commits to processing and safeguarding your personal data in compliance with the Personal Data Protection Law No. 6698 ("PDPL") and the EU General Data Protection Regulation ("GDPR") according to international standards. All your medical data is protected with end-to-end encryption.

2. Processed Data Categories

Identity and contact information; account and transaction security records; appointment and service records; where the user utilizes the relevant feature, health measurements, conditions, allergies, medications, laboratory, imaging, menstrual/pregnancy tracking and uploaded health documents; approximate/precise location if location permission is granted; support and communications records may be processed.

3. Purposes and Legal Grounds

For each processing activity, the appropriate processing condition under Article 5 of Law No. 6698, or Article 6 for health data, is defined in a separate data inventory. Explicit consent is collected solely for legally required and truly optional operations; it is never presented as a mandatory condition for service.

4. Data Transfers

If transfers are made to hosting, database, mapping, notification, communication, or AI service providers, the recipient, purpose, data categories, and destination country are maintained in the data inventory. Cross-border transfers of health data are never enabled without implementing appropriate safeguards under Article 9 of the PDPL.

5. Retention and Erasure

Data is retained only for the duration necessary for the specified purposes and statutory obligations. Retention periods are defined by data category in the data retention and disposal schedule; expired data is permanently deleted, destroyed, or anonymized.

6. Data Subject Rights

Users may exercise their rights under Article 11 of the PDPL by applying to the data controller. The in-app Privacy Center provides tools to view consent logs, export structured data, and initiate account and data deletion requests.
legal.termsHtml:
Platform Role

Alumas is a technology platform that facilitates access to healthcare services, physician/institution discovery, appointment booking, and user-selected health management tools. It is not a healthcare provider, emergency call center, or diagnostic/treatment provider.

Result Ranking

Matching algorithms may utilize explainable signals such as medical specialty alignment, proximity, availability, credential verification, facility status, and user preferences. Ranking does not constitute a guarantee of medical outcomes.

User Responsibility

In emergencies or acute medical conditions, immediate medical attention should not be delayed based on application results. Professional clinical evaluation is paramount.

Third-Party Services

Map, hosting, database, notification, and other integrations may be subject to their respective terms of service; personal data transfers remain subject to PDPL compliance processes.
legal.cookiesHtml:
Essential Technologies

Mandatory cookies and similar technologies may be deployed to facilitate secure authentication, security monitoring, and core application functions requested by the user.

Optional Technologies

Analytics and marketing technologies remain disabled by default and are activated strictly following explicit user consent. Preferences can be updated at any time in settings.

Third-Party Integrations

Before any third-party SDK or tracking tag is introduced, its purpose, vendor, retention period, and cross-border transfer impact are logged in our compliance inventory.
legal.providerTermsHtml:
Accuracy and Credentials

Professionals and healthcare institutions are strictly responsible for maintaining accurate and up-to-date credentials, specialties, licensure, and contact information. Alumas reserves the right to request proof of licensure and suspend unverified profiles.

Promotional Content Standards

Content that is misleading, claims absolute clinical superiority, guarantees medical outcomes, lacks scientific evidence, or violates medical advertising regulations is strictly prohibited. Moderation and audit mechanisms are continuously enforced.
legal.retentionHtml:
Fundamental Principle

For each personal data category, specific processing purposes, legal grounds, triggering lifecycle events, retention durations, and disposal methods are defined. Indefinite retention defaults are strictly barred.

Account and Data Erasure

A data subject's deletion request initiates the structured erasure workflow for records without statutory preservation requirements. Records mandated by healthcare regulations are transferred to restricted, compartmentalized retention archives.
legal.aiPolicyHtml:
Role of AI

Alumas AI is a healthcare navigation and informational tool; it is not a medical professional, does not establish diagnoses, does not issue prescriptions, and does not substitute for emergency medical care.

Sources and Explainability

Medical information is sourced strictly from verified clinical layers. Doctor and healthcare facility results originate from authenticated Alumas records and transparently labeled mapping providers. Users are provided with explicit references and rationale whenever navigation guidance is generated.

Emergency Handling

Upon detection of acute risk signals, normal discovery algorithms yield immediately to prominent emergency assistance workflows. Automated categorization is acknowledged to have technical limitations.

Mandatory Medical Notice

I am not a healthcare professional. This disclaimer is displayed prominently across all health responses.
legal.healthTourismHtml:
Authorization & Licensing

Should Alumas or an affiliated agency on the platform operate as an international health tourism intermediary organization, valid statutory authorization certificates and Ministry of Health compliance credentials must be verified prior to active listing.

Facility Profile & Digital Presence

Credentials, trade names, language capabilities, accreditations/certifications, and promotional responsibilities are monitored per facility classification. The platform strictly prohibits displaying unauthorized entities as authorized health tourism facilitators.
legal.crossBorderHtml:
Data Transfer Inventory

Prior to engaging international infrastructure providers such as Vercel, Neon, Google, or other vendors, data flows, provider roles, destination jurisdictions, data categories, and legal purposes are comprehensively documented.

Appropriate Safeguards

Adequacy decisions or appropriate safeguard mechanisms under Article 9 of the Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL) and GDPR are strictly evaluated. Standard contractual clauses are deployed in exact regulatory form without alteration, observing statutory filing deadlines following signature execution.
legal.healthDataPolicyTitle: Special Category Personal Data & Health Data Policy
legal.healthDataPolicyHtml:
Scope of Health Data

Information such as medical history, diagnoses, medications, allergies, laboratory/imaging records, pregnancy, and menstrual cycle data constitute special category personal data.

Product Principles

Data minimization, role-based access control, access audit logs, transfer limitations, and purpose limitation are strictly enforced. Health data is never used for marketing profiling. AI personalization is activated only by explicit user preference, and unnecessary raw health data is never transmitted to third-party models.

Additional Measures

In production, encryption at rest and in transit, key management, access permission reviews, comprehensive logging, incident response, backups, and breach procedures are executed under technical and administrative control checklists.
